name: Fennel White Bean and Kale Soup
description: Hearty soup with lots of veggie and protein.

instructions.text: Read the entire method first and measure the following ingredients before turning on the heat: ½ cup olive oil; 2 small fennel bulbs, small-diced; 2 small yellow onions, small-diced; 4 teaspoons minced fresh rosemary or thyme; 10 cloves of garlic, minced or pressed; ½-1 teaspoon red-pepper flakes.; 10-12 oz kale, (escarole, swiss chard, or spinach can also be used).; 4 cans cannellini beans, rinsed; 4 cups chicken broth.; 2 tablespoons lemon juice; 6 tablespoons grated parmesan, plus extra for serving if desired. Keep ingredients marked optional separate until their step.

Prepare these ingredients before cooking: Rosemary or thyme: minced fresh; Garlic: minced or pressed; Cannellini beans: rinsed; Parmesan: grated; plus extra for serving if desired. Wash produce under running water before cutting. Use a cutting board and a sharp knife; keep raw meat and its utensils separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.
In a large soup pot, heat olive oil over medium.
Add fennel, onion, rosemary and mix until tender (4-6 min).
Add garlic, red pepper flakes, cook until fragrant (1 min).
Add one handful of greens at a time, stirring until leaves wilt.
Add white beans, broth, and black pepper,
Bring to boil then bring to simmer while mashing some of the beans with a wooden spoon. A simmer means small, gentle bubbles; lower the burner if it boils vigorously.
Simmer until liquid has reduced and simmered (6-8 mins) A simmer means small, gentle bubbles; lower the burner if it boils vigorously.
Take off heat, stir in lemon juice and parmesan.

Before serving, insert a food thermometer into the thickest piece of chicken or turkey, away from bone: it must reach 165°F (74°C). If using already-cooked poultry, reheat it to 165°F (74°C). Continue cooking and recheck if needed; wash hands and utensils after handling raw poultry and do not rinse it.
Serve with some toasted bread that is good at scooping up soup.

Turn off any burners or oven when cooking is finished. Follow the cooling or resting instruction above before cutting or serving. Serve the finished dish as directed; allow hot portions to cool enough to eat.
